latest_n.title: The Home Depot
latest_n.summary:
The Home Depot's founding story is like an Avengers movie… if the Avengers got fired, went broke, and stacked empty paint cans ten feet high to look legitimate. After being unceremoniously fired from their previous hardware chain at ages 48 and 35, Bernie Marcus and Arthur Blank took the words of their New York banker Ken Langone (who had also just accidentally caused their firings) to heart: they'd just been "kicked in the ass with a golden horseshoe.” They proceeded to author the greatest compounding story in American retail history, helped by some legendary cameos along the way from Sol Price, Jamie Dimon, and Ross Perot (to name a few). And the ending is as good as any superhero film: from its 1981 IPO to today, The Home Depot has been the single highest-returning equity in the entire US stock market — higher than Apple, Microsoft, Berkshire Hathaway, and everything else!

latest_n.title: Disney: The Renaissance and the Empire
latest_n.summary:
In 1984, the Walt Disney Company was worth more dead than alive. Disney Animation — the heart of Walt's famous flywheel — had stagnated for years, bleeding away talent while corporate raiders circled, salivating over offers to sell off the film library to MGM and offload the parks to hotel operators. But what followed instead was the greatest turnaround in media history under Michael Eisner and Frank Wells. Beauty and the Beast. The Lion King. Broadway. Bringing the Disney Vault home on VHS and DVD. And the greatest media acquisition of all time — ESPN.
 And then... it all almost fell apart. Again. Euro Disney turned into a money pit. Boardroom and executive infighting ran rampant. Animation descended into a dumpster fire. (Remember Chicken Little? Us neither.) Comcast — Comcast!! — tried to steal the company via a hostile takeover. Out of the chaos, a new generation of Disney management emerged under Bob Iger to stage yet another epic comeback with Pixar, Marvel and Lucasfilm, creating the defining media empire of the 21st century…until the tech companies came along. Tune in for the ultimate Acquired thrill ride: Disney, Part II.

latest_n.title: The Walt Disney Company
latest_n.summary:
The Walt Disney Company is the most successful enterprise ever created for monetizing human nostalgia. Today it’s the king of global entertainment, holding the intellectual property rights to the childhood memories of billions of people (including, likely, all of you) and is a reliable, predictable profitable business. But it didn’t start that way.
 During Walt’s era, Disney operated like an unhinged moonshot factory, blowing its finances on one seemingly crazy project after another, like the very first feature-length animated film or a theme park inspired by Walt's fascination with model trains (spoiler: Disneyland). Walt’s relentless ambition to bet the company over and over again not only created some of the most monumental artistic achievements of the 20th century (Snow White, Fantasia, Disney Imagineering), but also resulted in the accidental invention of the modern “flywheel” business model. In this episode, we tell the story of the ultimate marriage of art, commerce, and engineering — The Walt Disney Company: Walt's Era.

latest_n.title: The Hacker Who Hunts Predators: Do These 3 Things Before You Get Hacked! | Ryan Montgomery
latest_n.summary:
What could a hacker find about you in just 20 minutes? Old passwords? Phone number? Childhood home? Ethical hacker Ryan Montgomery aka 0day reveals how exposed your personal data already is, and the simple moves that protect your online privacy.
Ryan Montgomery is an ethical hacker and cybersecurity expert who overcame addiction and jail as a teenager to become a go-to expert helping law enforcement unmask online predators. He is the founder of the cybersecurity company Pentester and works with the Sentinel Foundation on child-crime and counter-trafficking investigations. His tools are built on the same technology he uses to track predators, and they show ordinary people exactly what’s exposed about them online and then remove it.
In this episode, he explains:
■ The Reverse Password Trap: One unique old password leaked in a data breach lets hackers trace every other email account you’ve ever tied to it.
■ The Invisible Footprint: Even people who have never used a computer are exposed, because pharmacy sign-ups and hacked company databases feed data brokers who sell your address to anyone.
■ The Fake Free Wi-Fi: Hackers can create a fake public Wi-Fi network with a fake login page in seconds and capture your email and password the moment you sign in.
■ The Airplane Mode Myth: Airplane mode leaves Bluetooth switched on, so nearby attackers can still reach your phone unless you turn Bluetooth off in Settings.
■ The Smart Home Backdoor: Many cheap smart bulbs and plugs send your commands through overseas servers, so keep them on a separate network from your phone and laptop.
If you or someone you know has been affected by the issues in this episode, help is available. In the UK, contact the Samaritans on 116 123 or the NSPCC on 0808 800 5000. In the US, call or text 988, or report child exploitation to the NCMEC CyberTipline at report.cybertip.org. If a child is in immediate danger, call your local emergency number.

latest_n.title: Are We Living Through The Biggest AI Bubble In History? | Steve Eisman
latest_n.summary:
Are we on the verge of a catastrophic economic recession driven by the AI boom? Legendary investor Steve Eisman sits down to discuss market crashes, bubbles and the next financial crisis, revealing the driving force behind the AI hype and how everyday people can protect their wealth.
Steve Eisman is a renowned professional investor famously known for predicting the 2008 subprime mortgage collapse, a story immortalized in The Big Short. Today, he hosts a financial podcast and educational venture alongside his wife, Valerie. Through this platform, he aims to teach everyday people how to understand the markets without falling for Wall Street’s hype.
In this episode, he explains:
■ The Rule of Ruin: Human incentives will always trump ethics, which is the hidden catalyst behind every major financial collapse.
■ The AI Extinction Conspiracy: Tech billionaires are faking hysteria about AI ending the world simply to trigger government regulations that lock out their cheaper international competitors.
■ The Crypto Illusion: Cryptocurrency completely fails as an economic hedge because it moves directly in sync with tech stocks rather than protecting against inflation.
■ The Homeownership Trap: Buying a house is currently a terrible financial decision, and you are much better off renting while investing your extra cash into the stock market.
■ The Boring Secret to Wealth: Everyday people should completely avoid stock picking and instead consistently invest a portion of their income into the S&P 500 index fund for decades.
